title.en: Fix the tone in a neighbour dispute
title.es: Corregir el tono en un conflicto de vecinos

es: Localizar los errores de tono de un intercambio entre vecinos y redactar una respuesta reparadora en el registro adecuado, con disculpa y petición concreta.

vocabulary.es: aclarar las cosas, despejar la tensión
bajar el volumen, no hacer ruido

teaching.en: The note on my door was rude: it gave an order in capital letters, blamed me for every problem and did not even mention my name.
teaching.es: La nota en mi puerta era grosera: daba una orden en mayúsculas, me culpaba de todos los problemas y ni siquiera mencionaba mi nombre.
teaching.explanationEs: Rude: orden seca + acusación. Localizar el error de tono es el primer paso para repararlo.
segments: The note on my door was rude: it gave an order in capital
letters, blamed me for every problem and did not even mention my name.
teaching.audioText: The note on my door was rude: it gave an order in capital letters, blamed me for every problem and did not even mention my name.

teaching.en: A considerate reply begins with a sincere apology, such as I am sorry that the music disturbed you, and only then explains what happened.
teaching.es: Una respuesta considerada empieza con una disculpa sincera, como I am sorry that the music disturbed you, y solo después explica lo ocurrido.
teaching.explanationEs: Considerate: piensa en el otro; apology + I am sorry that + hecho, sin reproches.
segments: A considerate reply begins with a sincere apology, such as I am
sorry that the music disturbed you, and only then explains what happened.
teaching.audioText: A considerate reply begins with a sincere apology, such as I am sorry that the music disturbed you, and only then explains what happened.

teaching.en: A good complaint describes the problem instead of attacking the person, so avoid always and never, which sound like an attempt to blame.
teaching.es: Una buena queja describe el problema en lugar de atacar a la persona, así que evita always y never, que suenan a intento de culpar.
teaching.explanationEs: Complaint educada: hechos, no acusaciones; always y never culpan.
segments: A good complaint describes the problem instead of attacking the person, so
avoid always and never, which sound like an attempt to blame.
teaching.audioText: A good complaint describes the problem instead of attacking the person, so avoid always and never, which sound like an attempt to blame.

teaching.en: If your neighbour might take offence at a direct request, ask whether you could both keep it down after ten instead of telling them to stop.
teaching.es: Si tu vecino podría ofenderse ante una petición directa, pregunta si los dos podrían bajar el ruido después de las diez, en lugar de decirle que pare.
teaching.explanationEs: Take offence = ofenderse; keep it down = no hacer ruido. Could you both… incluye a los dos.
segments: If your neighbour might take offence at a direct request, ask whether you
could both keep it down after ten instead of telling them to stop.
teaching.audioText: If your neighbour might take offence at a direct request, ask whether you could both keep it down after ten instead of telling them to stop.

teaching.en: The best way to clear the air after an argument is to admit your part of the problem and to meet halfway on a practical solution.
teaching.es: La mejor manera de aclarar las cosas tras una discusión es admitir tu parte del problema y llegar a un punto intermedio con una solución práctica.
teaching.explanationEs: Clear the air + meet halfway: reparar la relación con una solución concreta.
segments: The best way to clear the air after an argument is to admit
your part of the problem and to meet halfway on a practical solution.
teaching.audioText: The best way to clear the air after an argument is to admit your part of the problem and to meet halfway on a practical solution.

teaching.en: Do not put but straight after an apology: «I'm sorry, but you started it» cancels the apology, whereas «I am sorry that the noise disturbed you» keeps it sincere.
teaching.es: No pongas but justo después de una disculpa: «Lo siento, pero tú empezaste» la anula, mientras que «Lamento que el ruido le molestara» la mantiene sincera.
teaching.explanationEs: But anula la disculpa; I am sorry that… + hecho la conserva.
segments: Do not put but straight after an apology: «I'm sorry, but you started it» cancels
the apology, whereas «I am sorry that the noise disturbed you» keeps it sincere.
teaching.audioText: Do not put but straight after an apology: «I'm sorry, but you started it» cancels the apology, whereas «I am sorry that the noise disturbed you» keeps it sincere.

prompt.es: Localiza los dos errores de tono de la nota del vecino.

choices.text: An order in capital letters, and a reproach with «always».
A sarcastic comment, and an offer to find a solution together.
A formal greeting, and a long apology that never mentions the problem.

feedback.es: La orden en mayúsculas y el «always» que culpa son los dos errores de tono que hay que localizar y reparar.

hint.es: Mira el imperativo con mayúsculas y la palabra que generaliza la culpa.

origin.text: Your music is too loud. You always do this, and I am tired of it. Turn it down NOW!

prompt.es: Completa: «Lleguemos a un punto intermedio y acordemos una hora de silencio.»

feedback.es: Meet halfway significa ceder los dos un poco para llegar a un acuerdo; es la base de una respuesta reparadora.

hint.es: Adverbio que significa «a mitad de camino».

origin.text: I would like to clear the air, so let us meet ___ and agree on a quiet hour after ten.

prompt.es: Ordena la petición cortés: «¿Podrías bajar el volumen después de las diez?»

answer.text: Could you keep it down after ten

feedback.es: Could you + keep it down es una petición cortés que describe la acción sin acusar a nadie.

hint.es: Empieza por Could you y termina con la hora.

prompt.es: Elige la respuesta que repara el tono sin culpar ni rendirse del todo.

choices.text: I'm sorry, but he is only a dog, and you should not take offence so easily when a dog barks.
I am sorry that the barking disturbed you. Could we meet halfway and agree on a time when he stays inside?
You are right, and I will give my dog away immediately, since I can never stop him barking.

feedback.es: Solo una respuesta pide perdón sin but, describe el problema y propone una solución concreta a medias.

origin.text: Your dog barks all day! If you don't do something about it, I will report you. You never listen to anything I say!

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hizo la vecina para que él no se ofendiera.

choices.text: She said she would call the police unless he stopped immediately.
She blamed him for every night of noise since he had arrived.
She described the effect on her baby and proposed an agreement, calmly.

feedback.es: La vecina explica el efecto en su bebé y propone un acuerdo con calma: no amenaza ni culpa.

origin.audio: Yesterday my neighbour came to my door. She did not shout, but she said: I'm sure you don't realise, but the music after midnight has kept my baby awake three nights this week. I felt a little annoyed at first, yet her tone was calm, and she added: I wonder if we could agree on a time when it goes off? I apologised at once and offered to keep it down after ten. Without such a considerate approach, I would probably have taken offence.

prompt.es: Reescribe la nota con un tono cortés y sin acusaciones.

answer.text: Could you keep the music down after ten, please? I find it hard to sleep when it is loud.
accepted: Could you keep the music down after ten, please? I find it hard to sleep when it is loud.
Would you mind turning the music down after ten? It is difficult for me to sleep when it is loud.
Could you please turn the music down after ten? I find it difficult to sleep when it is loud.

feedback.es: Una petición cortés con could you + hora concreta y la causa descrita sin acusar sustituye a la orden y al always.

origin.text: Turn the music down NOW! You always make noise at night.

evidenceGroups: i was wondering if you could

prompt.es: ¿Qué estrategia usa Mia en su respuesta al vecino?

choices.text: She apologises, avoids blaming him and offers a specific limit.
She apologises, then explains why he was wrong to complain.
She accepts all the blame and promises never to play music again.

feedback.es: Mia pide perdón sin but, no acusa y fija un límite concreto (las diez): disculpa, problema y petición.

origin.text: Dear Mr Hill, I am sorry that the music disturbed you last night. I did not mean to bother anyone. Could we agree that it will stay low after ten? Thank you for your understanding. Kind regards, Mia

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz: ¿qué actitud revela realmente el hablante?

choices.text: He is pleased with his neighbour and sincerely thanks him for the music.
He is really annoyed, and his thanks are sarcastic.
He is tentative and politely asks the neighbour to continue.

feedback.es: Las frases amables contradicen la situación (una noche sin dormir): el agradecimiento es sarcasmo, no cortesía.

origin.audio: Oh, lovely. Another night of loud music until two in the morning. Thanks so much; that is exactly how I wanted to start my week. Please, do carry on.

prompt.es: Completa: «Carlos escribió una nota para aclarar las cosas tras la discusión.»

feedback.es: Clear the air significa despejar la tensión tras un conflicto, hablando de ello con sinceridad.

origin.text: After the argument, Carlos wrote a short note to try to ___ the air. He began with an apology and offered to keep the music down after ten.

prompt.es: Repara el conflicto: localiza dos errores y responde (170-220 palabras).

answer.text: The note has two tone problems: it gives a rude order in capital letters, and it blames me with the word always. Here is my reply. Dear Mr Hill, I am sorry that the music disturbed you last night, and I understand that it is hard to sleep when there is noise. I would like to clear the air and find a solution together. From now on I will keep the music down after ten every evening, and I will remind my guests of the rule as well. Could we meet halfway and agree on that? I hope that this is convenient for you. Thank you for telling me about the problem so clearly, and please let me know if anything else bothers you. Kind regards, Carlos
accepted: The note has two tone problems: it gives a rude order in capital letters, and it blames me with the word always. Here is my reply. Dear Mr Hill, I am sorry that the music disturbed you last night, and I understand that it is hard to sleep when there is noise. I would like to clear the air and find a solution together. From now on I will keep the music down after ten every evening, and I will remind my guests of the rule as well. Could we meet halfway and agree on that? I hope that this is convenient for you. Thank you for telling me about the problem so clearly, and please let me know if anything else bothers you. Kind regards, Carlos

The note is rude for two reasons: the order in capital letters, and the word always, which blames me for everything. My reply: Dear Mr Hill, I apologise that my music disturbed you. I know that noise at night makes it hard to sleep, and I would like to clear the air. I would like to suggest a solution: from now on I will keep it down after ten, and my friends will know the rule too. If you prefer another time, we can meet halfway and agree on it together. Would that be convenient for you? Thank you very much for being so patient with me, and please tell me if there is any other problem. Yours sincerely, Carlos

feedback.es: Una respuesta reparadora localiza el tono, empieza con una disculpa sin but, describe el problema y fija una solución concreta.

origin.text: Caso: tu vecino, Mr Hill, te dejó esta nota: «Your music is terrible!! Turn it down NOW, you always do this!». Escribe: 1) los dos errores de tono de la nota; 2) una respuesta formal con disculpa, el problema, una solución y una petición concreta (bajar la música a las diez).

prompt.es: ¿Qué respuesta repara el tono sin acusar ni ceder en todo?

choices.text: I'm sorry, but children are noisy, and you should not take offence so easily when they play at home.
You are right, and I will stop my children from playing at home at all, from today.
I am sorry that the noise has disturbed you. Could we agree on quiet hours after eight and meet halfway?

feedback.es: La respuesta correcta empieza con una disculpa sin but, no acusa al vecino y propone horas concretas y un punto medio.

origin.text: To the people in flat three: the noise from your children is far too loud. I suppose nobody ever taught them to be quiet. Please do something, or I will speak to the landlord.

prompt.es: Completa: «Podría ofenderse si le dices directamente que pare.»

feedback.es: Take offence es la colocación para ofenderse; se evita empezando con una disculpa en lugar de una orden.

origin.text: Your neighbour has been quiet about the noise so far, but he might take ___ if you tell him directly to stop. Start with an apology instead.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Lamento que el ruido le molestara anoche.»

answer.text: I am sorry that the noise disturbed you last night

feedback.es: I am sorry that + hecho expresa una disculpa sincera sin reproches ni but.
